speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether any recent patterns have been observed in scams targeting seniors; and (b) if so, what these patterns are.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
text: And we have explained in this House before why the recovery of scam proceeds is very challenging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Once the monies exit Singapore, the odds of it being recovered is very low.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Member may wish to refer to the Annual Scam and Cybercrime Brief 2025 for more details on these recovery initiatives.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One, given the increasing sophistication of scams targeting seniors, including cross-border and multi-step operations, could the Minister of State share how Singapore is strengthening its overall system design to stay ahead of rapidly evolving scam typologies rather than responding only after patterns emerge?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Two, could the Minister of State also share how coordination across banks, telecommunication companies (telcos) and enforcement agencies is being further optimised to shorten the critical time between scam detection and intervention, including the freezing of funds or disruption of scam flows, given how quickly losses can occur once victims are engaged?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And three, beyond systems and enforcement, could the Minister of State share how Singapore is further strengthening safeguards against increasingly sophisticated social engineering tactics that exploit trust, urgency and fear, particularly among our seniors, so that we can better protect vulnerable individuals before irreversible financial harm occurs?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I will try to take them together as one reply.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And the financial incentive for scammers and for perpetrators is immense and therefore, they will try their very best to continuously innovate and get ahead.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: But having said so, indeed, I fully agree with what the Member has raised, in terms of the key thrusts that we should adopt in our anti-scam strategy – being proactive, going upstream, taking a risk-based approach and collaborating with partners.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think these are all very useful perspectives.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And indeed, that is the approach that we have taken as a whole-of-Government and a whole-of-society anti-scam strategy, multi-agency and multi-pronged.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And let me take the chance to share some of the key thrusts of how we have approached this problem.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We are working very closely with our online service providers to make sure we reduce the overall threat surface area that these platforms put on.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Second, we work very closely with our telcos, our banks and also the recognised and authorised crypto service providers to make sure we are able to prevent upstream as well as interdict after scams have taken place.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Third, we have also enhanced our penalty framework to deter perpetrators from operating in Singapore and also making sure that we work closely with overseas partners to pursue overseas where possible.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We have also put in place a penalty framework to deter scam mules.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Fourth, public education – extensive public education, including for our seniors – to make sure that we share the latest modus operandi as well as the best anti-scam preventive practices that our citizens and our seniors can adopt.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And fifth, we are stepping up international collaboration with governments, with jurisdictions, with law enforcement agencies sharing best practices as well as making sure we cooperate and share intelligence closely and to also shape how global norms approach scams.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think we have taken a very extensive approach.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Of course, we can do more and we want to continuously spare no effort in making sure we fight scams.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I would also like to refer the Member to the Home Affairs Ministry's Committee of Supply debate speech just a few months ago.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We have given a fuller account of all the various initiatives that we have taken and will be taking to fight scams.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And of course, we welcome any further suggestions the Member may have.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just a question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Ministry capture the total amount of monies recovered from Singaporeans who are victims of scams?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I believe, earlier, the Minister of State said that the Police does not collect that information, but I am wondering whether that was specific to the different age groups?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Police or the Ministry have a global figure of how much actually has been recovered?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because that may help Singaporeans understand that if you are a victim of scams, the prospect of recovering your money is actually very low.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We just do not track them by age group.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I do not have the exact figures, but it is a smaller percentage.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And I think that is also a useful reminder that, indeed, prevention is better than the follow-up pursuit of recovering monies.
